findings.title: Strict DTO shapes diverge from the frozen accepted API contract
findings.reproduction: The first three independent probes reject valid frozen objects: approvalAudit {eventId,createdAt} is replaced by {id,action,createdAt}; PrivateDraftReview requires an unallocated previewProjectId; ReviewCheck rejects the explicitly allocated site scope/generic id. The current schema is internally coherent for its own output, but that does not satisfy exact DTO ownership.
findings.impact: Downstream consumers of the accepted DTO cannot parse/submit the prescribed shapes. No publish authorization bypass is claimed.

findings.title: Healthy publication refresh always fails because client and API response keys disagree
findings.reproduction: Actual owner GET /api/admin/publish returns200 with currentRevision,activePublication,history,authorizedActor. Both refreshReview and refreshAfterCommit require publicationResponse.publication, which is absent. The corresponding independent API probe fails. The supplied rollback screenshot already shows active r3, reviewed expected r1, incomplete refresh feedback, and a stale-review prompt.
findings.impact: Refresh review cannot recover stale publication identity. After successful publish/rollback the in-page review remains stale and publishing is disabled until page reload. The browser test forces one failed refresh and checks only committed feedback thereafter, allowing this real failure to pass.

findings.title: Missing genuine private draft throws before the intended not-found branches
findings.reproduction: An authenticated owner requesting the known CandidateX ID with an empty explicit draft registry receives503. A requested-project review requires exactly one draft; with none it throws before the API404 check and before page notFound(). The API result is directly reproduced; the page exception path is source inspection, not an independent browser run.
findings.impact: Ordinary absence is reported as temporary backend failure; the page cannot reach its not-found path. Denial and privacy headers still pass.

findings.title: Authorized stale-save conflicts omit the required current draft identity and content
findings.reproduction: Save a fixture with current revision2 using expectedRevision1. The owner receives409 with only error and code; no current project/title or current draft/review identity is returned. The independent test logs the entire response and fails the current-content assertion.
findings.impact: The documented authorized conflict handoff is missing even though the unsaved buffer remains intact and durable writes reject. No unauthorized content exposure is claimed.

findings.title: Draft image renderer accepts absolute and traversal-containing URLs
findings.reproduction: Independent React server rendering emits img for both http://yor-world.local/api/admin/preview/media/fixture and /discard/../api/admin/preview/media/fixture. The helper validates normalized origin/path but renders the original string; neither is the exact allowed relative URL.
findings.impact: The required narrow renderer boundary is not enforced. Current server media resolver supplies the safe relative path, so no route-auth bypass, XSS or attacker-controlled production URL exploit was reproduced.

findings.title: New authoring inputs still invent valid nonempty content and link check dates
findings.reproduction: Source directly inserts New Section/New section content., New paragraph., and New list item as valid nonempty project content. Add link also inserts Documentation + https://example.com/docs + checkedAt=now without asking for a real record. New evidence correctly uses unknown/null, but the other defaults do not follow the accepted instruction to request real content.
findings.impact: These invented values can be saved and reviewed as ordinary authored content without being replaced; existing checks validate structure/record syntax and do not distinguish these generated values. This is a source finding; no independent additional browser execution is claimed.
